reviewA: As a returning reader, I am watching for the author's tics, especially regarding the Ruliad and Borges. Post A combines both, which initially sent up a red flag—the author linking his two primary obsessions again. However, the move he makes here is genuinely novel. Instead of treating the Ruliad as a purely ontological problem, he applies it to *belief*. Framing belief as 'a position in a space of possibilities. A moving window,' and defining the 'belief engine' not as deception but as 'how any world comes to exist' through repetition, is a new, lateral connection. The closing move—distinguishing the labyrinth as 'a school of walking' rather than a trap—feels like a genuine update to his earlier, more fatalistic interpretations of Borges's infinite spaces. He is still using his familiar toolbox, but he is building a different shape with it.
reviewB: Post B, on the other hand, is the author firmly at rest. We have another Borges story ('The Aleph') set to a Brazilian regional form (Cateretê), which exactly parallels the move made in 'O Telefone da Agonia' (moda de viola). The narrative structure—a comic interaction between the cynical narrator and the oblivious Carlos Argentino—is structurally identical to previous posts about this same story. Even the attempt to elevate the comedic premise to a philosophical stance in the notes ('A preguiça como posição filosófica' linked back to process ontology) feels like a generic 'franklin-blog' auto-pilot move. It’s competent, the lyrics are clever, but there is absolutely nothing happening here that the author hasn't already done in the last five posts. It is generic competence in his own voice.
clash: Which post moves the author forward, vs. which post is the author at rest? Post B is practically a template execution: Borges reference + Brazilian folk form + cynical narrator + a tacked-on note about process ontology. It is indistinguishable in structure from other entries in the Borges cycle. Post A risks falling into the same trap by invoking the Ruliad and Borges together, but it escapes by making a novel conceptual leap, applying the physics of the Ruliad to the mechanics of human belief. The insight that repetition creates reality ('the more we agree on a story, the heavier it gets') within the computational space is a fresh lateral connection for this blog. Post A is the author working out a new idea; Post B is the author playing the hits. Post A, 4.10 to 3.20.
afterMood: Sinto o gosto do café enfraquecendo na boca, hora de levantar e esticar as pernas de verdade.
